text_en: The euro currency is established, and the European Central Bank assumes full powers.
The Mars Polar Lander is launched by NASA.
American crime drama series The Sopranos premieres on HBO, beginning what many commentators describe as the second “Golden Age of Television”.
The 6.2 Mw Colombia earthquake strikes western Colombia, killing at least 1,900 people.
Abdullah II inherits the throne of Jordan, following the death of his father, King Hussein.
Pluto moves along its eccentric orbit further from the Sun than Neptune. It had been nearer than Neptune since 1979, and will become again in 2231.
U.S. President Bill Clinton is acquitted in impeachment proceedings in the United States Senate.
While trying to circumnavigate the world in a hot air balloon, Colin Prescot and Andy Elson set a new endurance record after being aloft for 233 hours and 55 minutes.
Former Warsaw Pact members Hungary, Poland, and the Czech Republic join NATO.
The Santer Commission of the EU resigns over allegations of corruption.
The Melissa virus attacks the Internet.
Kosovo War: A U.S. Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk is shot down by Yugoslav forces.
The adult animated sitcom Futurama premiered on Fox.
For the first time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closes above the 10,000 mark, at 10,006.78.
Nunavut, an Inuit homeland, is created from the eastern portion of the Northwest Territories to become Canada's third territory.
Kosovo War: Kosovo's main border crossings are closed by Yugoslav forces to prevent Kosovo Albanians from leaving.
Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara, president of Niger, is assassinated.

Kosovo War: NATO warplanes repeatedly bomb ethnic Albanian refugee convoys for 2 hours over a 12-mile stretch of road, after mistaking them for Yugoslav military trucks, between Đakovica and Dečani in western Kosovo, killing at least 73 refugees.

Columbine High School massacre: 14 people, including 13 students[a] and one teacher, are killed in a mass shooting and attempted bombing at a high school in Columbine, Colorado; 23 others are injured by the two student perpetrators, who then kill themselves.
Cambodia joins the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), bringing the total members to 10.
Children's animated television series SpongeBob SquarePants premieres on Nickelodeon.

1999 Oklahoma tornado outbreak: a devastating tornado, rated F5 on the Fujita scale, hits southern and eastern Oklahoma City metropolitan area, killing 36 people (and 5 indirectly) and producing the highest winds recorded on Earth: 301 ± 20 mph (484 ± 32 km/h).
Mother's Day bus crash: a charter bus veers off the roadway before colliding with a dirk embankment in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States, killing 22 passengers and injuring another 22.
David Steel becomes the first Presiding Officer (Speaker) of the modern Scottish Parliament.
Carlo Azeglio Ciampi is elected President of Italy.
June 20 – The 1999 Cricket World Cup is held in England, (some matches in Scotland, Ireland, Wales and the Netherlands), with Australia defeating Pakistan in the final.
Ehud Barak is elected prime minister of Israel.
The WWF pay-per-view event Over the Edge takes place at Kemper Arena in Kansas City, Missouri. The event is tragically remembered for the accidental death of wrestler Owen Hart during a stunt.
Nigeria terminates military rule, and the Fourth Nigerian Republic is established with Olusegun Obasanjo as president.
The King of Bhutan allows television transmissions to commence in the Kingdom for the first time, coinciding with the King's Silver Jubilee.
The Islamic Salvation Army, the armed wing of the Islamic Salvation Front, agrees in principle to disband in Algeria.
The government of Colombia announces it will include the estimated value of the country's illegal drug crops, exceeding half a billion US dollars, in its gross national product.
Kosovo War: Yugoslavia and NATO sign a peace treaty to end their hostilities.
Kosovo War: NATO suspends its airstrikes after Slobodan Milošević agrees to withdraw Yugoslav forces from Kosovo.
Kosovo War: Operation Joint Guardian/Operation Agricola begins: NATO-led United Nations peacekeeping forces KFOR enter Kosovo, Yugoslavia.
Thabo Mbeki is inaugurated as the second president of South Africa, marking the first peaceful transfer of executive power in the country's post-democratization history.[importance?]
The J18 international anti-globalization protests are organized in dozens of cities around the world, some of which led to riots.
Turin, Italy, is awarded the 2006 Winter Olympics.
Australia defeats Pakistan by 8 wickets at Lord's Cricket Ground in London in the 1999 Cricket World Cup Final, securing their second World Cup title.
Kosovo War: NATO marines shoot three gunmen in Kosovo, Yugoslavia after being attacked by the latter, killing one of them and injuring the other two.
Bosnia and Herzegovina gets a new national anthem.
Twenty-three people die in a fire at the Sealand Youth Training Center in South Korea.
Europol (short for European Police Office) the European Union's criminal intelligence agency becomes fully operational.
In Rome, Hicham El Guerrouj runs the fastest mile ever recorded, at 3:43.13.
American soccer player Brandi Chastain scores the game winning penalty kick against China in the final of the FIFA Women's World Cup.
India recaptures Kargil, forcing the Pakistani army to retreat. India announces victory, ending the 2-month conflict.
the Big Blue crane collapse happened during the construction of Miller Park, killing three iron workers.
T-Mobile Park (formerly known as Safeco Field) opens for the first time.
John F. Kennedy Jr. dies in a plane crash off Martha's Vineyard.
MLB Pitcher David Cone of the New York Yankees, throws the 16th perfect game in Major League Baseball history.

25 – Woodstock '99 was held in Rome, New York at former Griffiss Air Force Base, which was marred with difficult environmental conditions, poor sanitation, overpriced food and water, looting, violence, rapes, riots and several deaths.
Twenty-one people die in a canyoning disaster at the Saxetenbach Gorge near Interlaken, Switzerland.
NASA intentionally crashes the Lunar Prospector spacecraft into the Moon, thus ending its mission to detect frozen water on the lunar surface.
Dagestan incursions: Hundreds of Chechen guerrillas invade the Russian republic of Dagestan, triggering the short war.
The Atlantique incident occurs as an intruding Pakistan Navy plane is shot down in India, sparking tensions between the two nations, a month after the end of the Kargil War.
A total solar eclipse is seen in Europe and Asia.
The 7.6 Mw İzmit earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), leaving more than 17,000 dead and around 50,000 injured.
In Belgrade, tens of thousands of Yugoslavs rally to demand the resignation of Yugoslav President Slobodan Milošević.
WWE introduce their secondary program, SmackDown, which started its broadcast on UPN.
East Timor votes for independence from Indonesia (which had invaded and occupied it since 1975) in a referendum.
The 1999 Ontario Highway 401 crash occurs, involving 87 vehicles and killing 8.
The 6.0 Mw Athens earthquake hits with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing 143, injuring 800–1,600, and leaving 50,000 homeless.
The first of a series of Russian apartment bombings occurs. Subsequent bombings occur on September 13 and 16, while a bombing on September 22 fails.
Sega releases the Dreamcast in North America, marking the launch of its final home video game console.
Under international pressure to allow an international peacekeeping force, Indonesian president BJ Habibie announces that he will do so.
Kiribati, Nauru and Tonga join the United Nations.
Start of the 1999 Greek stock market crash.
The 7.7 Mw 921 earthquake (also known as the Jiji earthquake) affects central Taiwan with a maximum Mercali intensity of X (Extreme) leaving 2,400 people dead and more than 11,000 injured.
NASA permanently loses contact with the Mars Climate Orbiter during orbital insertion around Mars, resulting in the spacecraft's loss and the failure of the mission.

Shanghai Pudong International Airport opens in China, becoming the primary international airport serving Shanghai and taking over all international flights from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport.
November 6 – The 1999 Rugby World Cup, the first World Cup in the professional era of rugby is held in Wales and is won by Australia who beat France in the final.
Thirty-one people die in the Ladbroke Grove rail crash, west of London, England.
Telenovela Yo soy Betty, la fea debuts on RCN Televisión in Colombia. It will give rise to Ugly Betty and at least a dozen other versions worldwide.
Armenian parliament shooting: Gunmen open fire in Armenia's National Assembly building, killing Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan, Parliament Chairman Karen Demirchyan, and six other members.
1999 Odisha cyclone: A super cyclonic storm impacts Orissa, India, killing approximately 10,000 people.
1999 Incheon bar fire [ko]: A bar catches fire in Incheon, South Korea, killing 56 people.
Australians defeat a referendum proposing the replacement of the Queen and the Governor General with a President to make Australia a republic.
The 7.2 Mw Düzce earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 845 people are killed and almost 5,000 are injured.
China launches the first Shenzhou spacecraft.
The National Assembly of Kuwait revokes a 1985 law that granted women's suffrage.
The 7.5 Mw Ambrym earthquake shakes Vanuatu and a destructive tsunami follows, killing 10 and injuring 40.
The centre-left Labour Party takes control of the New Zealand Government, with leader Helen Clark becoming the second female Prime Minister in New Zealand's history.
Bolivian municipal elections, the first election contested by Evo Morales' Movimiento al Socialismo.
The hormone Ghrelin is discovered and named.
NASA launches the Terra platform into orbit, carrying five Earth Observation instruments, including ASTER, CERES, MISR, MODIS and MOPITT.
Handover of Macau: the Portuguese Republic transfers administration of Macau to the People's Republic of China after 442 years of Portuguese rule in the settlement.
Indian Airlines Flight 814 was hijacked on 24 December 1999 by five members of Harkat-ul-Mujahideen in what was considered to be India's worst and last plane hijacking
Cyclone Lothar kills 140 people as it crosses France, southern Germany, and Switzerland.
A day after Cyclone Lothar, Cyclone Martin causes additional damage throughout France, Spain, Switzerland and Italy, including an emergency due to flooding at the Blayais Nuclear Power Plant.
